words.gloss: those things which are not real

literal: Reality not-being-those-things as reality thus perceiving by-delusion arises ignoble birth.
translation: From the delusion that perceives things which are not real as real, arises the ignoble cycle of birth.
modern: மெய்ப்பொருள் அல்லாதவற்றை மெய்ப்பொருள் என்று தவறாக உணர்கின்ற அறியாமையினால், சிறப்பற்ற பிறவித் துன்பம் உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the root cause of the cycle of rebirth and suffering. The key word 'maruḷ' (delusion) refers to the mental darkness that mistakes transient, unreal things ('poruḷ allavaṟṟai') for the eternal, ultimate truth ('poruḷ'). When a person perceives the illusory world as the ultimate reality, they develop attachments. This delusion leads to 'māṇā piṟappu' (ignoble or worthless birth), which represents the continuous cycle of rebirths filled with suffering.
